newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan needs to strengthen bank penalties-Hashimoto.
newsitem.headline: Japan needs to strengthen bank penalties-Hashimoto.

text.p: Japan needs stronger penalties for financial institutions which commit illegal acts, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday.

"In order to build a fairer financial market, there is a need to deal severely with illegal acts and to strengthen penalties against those who break the rules," Hashimoto said in a speech read out by deputy chief cabinet secretary Teijiro Furukawa on his behalf at a bankers' conference.

Hashimoto also said it was "truly regrettable" that a bank and a brokerage had allegedly paid off a corporate racketeer, adding it undermined the trust that depositors and investors had placed in the financial firms.

Hashimoto urged financial institutions to embrace good corporate morals and called on managers to carry out business appropriately, taking into account the banking industry's responsibility to the public.
At the same time, the banking industry needs to quickly take steps to prevent a recurrence of such incidents and to cut any links with the corporate racketeers, Hashimoto said.
The scandal has led to more than a dozen arrests of officials from Nomura Securities Co Ltd and one of Japan's biggest banks, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd.

Japan's "Big Bang" reforms, aimed at boosting competition in the industry and its markets, are needed to boost the yen's profile globally and to retain the Japanese economy's vitality amid the challenge of an ageing society, Hashimoto said.
The reforms will allow consumers to choose a variety of products and services and efficiently manage their assets.
Financial institutions are expected to strengthen their competitiveness and management base under this environment, Hashimoto said.
